subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw keep the legacy Chrome extension relay retired, restore it as a first-party optional path, or design a secure browser-backend/plugin API that can host an optional cross-machine relay?
rationale: The remaining work crosses both product direction and browser-control security boundaries, so automation cannot safely decide by restoring the old driver string or accepting the current migration as enough.

options.title: Design secure backend API plus relay
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved browser backend/plugin contract and implement a relay with explicit tab ownership, consent, auditing, migration, docs, and security tests.

options.title: Keep relay retired
options.body: Document that cross-machine browser control must use node hosts or remote CDP and close relay-specific restoration requests after that decision is explicit.

options.title: Restore first-party optional relay
options.body: Reintroduce the old-style relay as a maintained optional driver, accepting the core maintenance and security-review burden directly in OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Design secure backend API plus relay
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved browser backend/plugin contract and implement a relay with explicit tab ownership, consent, auditing, migration, docs, and security tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the removal and migration PR and has the strongest recent history on the browser driver/config seam.
